# bssd

bssd computes the posterior probability of a safety signal from blinded
clinical trial data, in which the treatment groups of the subjects with
an adverse event are unknown, with published Bayesian methods. The
posterior quantities are obtained by numerical integration instead of
Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, so the results do not depend
on a random seed and are fast enough for simulation studies.

## Models and functions

| Model | Blinded data | Function | Tested quantity |
|----|----|----|----|
| BDRIBS(1) (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018; Duncan, 2026) | number of subjects with the event and total exposure time | [`bdribs_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_post.md) | rate ratio |
| BDRIBS(2) (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018; Duncan, 2026) | number of subjects with the event and total time at risk | [`bdribs_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_post.md) | rate ratio |
| BINBETA (Ball and Schnell, 2016) | numbers of subjects and of subjects with the event | [`binbeta_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/binbeta_post.md) | study drug proportion or ratio |
| MULTIBIN (Goren et al., 2020) | the same, for each of several studies | [`multibin_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/multibin_post.md) | common rate ratio |
| CANARY (Gould and Wang, 2017) | total event count, with external control data | [`canary_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/canary_post.md) | ratio, difference or odds ratio |
| EXP_BERN (Duncan, 2026) | event indicator and follow-up time of each subject | [`expbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/expbern_post.md) | rate ratio |
| LL_BERN (Duncan, 2026) | event indicator and follow-up time of each subject | [`llbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/llbern_post.md) | ratio of the cumulative incidences at `t_star` |
| EXPTIME (Schnell and Ball, 2016) | number of events and follow-up time of each subject | [`exptime_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/exptime_post.md) | study drug rate or rate ratio |
| MAPBERN (Brock et al., 2023) | event indicator and time at risk of each subject, historical control arms | [`mapbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/mapbern_post.md), [`map_beta()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/map_beta.md) | ratio of the event probabilities |
| BDRIBS monitoring (Waterhouse et al., 2022) | as BDRIBS, on grids of data and for pooled trials | [`bdribs_grid()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_grid.md), [`pooled_ratio()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/pooled_ratio.md) | rate ratio |

BDRIBS is the Poisson-based model of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018), with
the total exposure time or the total time at risk as specified by Duncan
(2026); with `pt_hp = Inf`,
[`bdribs_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_post.md)
performs the screening analysis of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) with a
known background rate. The posterior functions (`*_post()`) return
objects with [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) and
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) methods.

Other functions:

- [`signal_count()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/signal_count.md):
  smallest event count with a signal for a number of subjects (decision
  boundaries and control charts).
- [`count_oc()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/count_oc.md):
  exact probability that the event count reaches the boundary.
- [`elicit_prior()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/elicit_prior.md):
  parameters of a Gamma, Beta or lognormal prior from two quantiles.
- [`time_at_risk()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/time_at_risk.md):
  total exposure time and total time at risk from subject-level data.
- [`ll_cdf()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/ll_cdf.md)
  and
  [`ll_mu()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/ll_mu.md):
  cumulative incidence and location parameter of the log-logistic
  distribution.
- [`sim_blinded()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/sim_blinded.md):
  simulation of blinded trial data.
- [`sim_oc()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/sim_oc.md):
  operating characteristics of the models by simulation.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/bssd")
```

## Examples

Hypothetical example 2 of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018, Section 4.4) has 9
subjects with the event in 540 patient-years of blinded exposure, a 2:1
randomization, and a known background rate of 0.011 per patient-year on
placebo.

``` r

library(bssd)
fit <- bdribs_post(y = 9, exposure = 540, k = 2, lambda_hp = 0.011,
                   pt_hp = Inf, p_prior = c(1, 1))
fit
#> Model: BDRIBS 
#> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo
#> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.753
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of r: mean 1.522, median 1.438, 95% interval (0.379, 3.143)
```

The posterior probability of r \> 1 is 0.753. The article reports 0.756,
computed by MCMC with the bdribs package.

The four models applied to simulated subject-level data (150 subjects,
1:1 randomization, log-logistic times to the event, analysis at week
117):

``` r

set.seed(2026)
d <- sim_blinded(n = 150, k = 1, accrual = 26, follow_up = 104,
                 analysis_time = 117, dist = "loglogistic",
                 par_p = c(7.3, 0.8), par_d = c(5.85, 0.8))
tar <- time_at_risk(d$follow_up, d$event, d$event_time)
lambda_hp <- -log(1 - ll_cdf(104, mu = 7.3, sigma = 0.8)) / 104
pt_weeks <- 75 * 104
fits <- list(
  BDRIBS1 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]], exposure = tar[["exposure"]],
                        k = 1, lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks,
                        df = 2),
  BDRIBS2 = bdribs_post(y = tar[["n_event"]],
                        exposure = tar[["time_at_risk"]], k = 1,
                        lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2),
  EXP_BERN = expbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1,
                          lambda_hp = lambda_hp, pt_hp = pt_weeks, df = 2),
  LL_BERN = llbern_post(y = d$event, t = d$follow_up, k = 1, mu_hp = 7.3,
                        sigma_hp = 0.8, pt_hp = pt_weeks / 52, df_p = 2,
                        t_star = 104)
)
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, summary))
res$model <- names(fits)
res[, c("model", "prob", "signal", "rr_median", "error")]
#>             model      prob signal rr_median        error
#> BDRIBS1   BDRIBS1 0.7909268  FALSE  2.879204           NA
#> BDRIBS2   BDRIBS2 0.8049487  FALSE  3.030938           NA
#> EXP_BERN EXP_BERN 0.8202782  FALSE  3.242507 1.180896e-07
#> LL_BERN   LL_BERN 0.9351465  FALSE  4.217216 3.733315e-04
```

[`vignette("bssd")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/bssd.md)
gives an overview of the models, the priors of this example and the
simulation of the operating characteristics. The articles
[`vignette("bdribs1")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/bdribs1.md),
[`vignette("bdribs2")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/bdribs2.md),
[`vignette("bdribs-monitoring")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/bdribs-monitoring.md),
[`vignette("binbeta")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/binbeta.md),
[`vignette("canary")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/canary.md),
[`vignette("expbern")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/expbern.md),
[`vignette("llbern")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/llbern.md),
[`vignette("exptime")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/exptime.md)
and
[`vignette("mapbern")`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/mapbern.md)
describe each model, with examples, the accuracy of the numerical
integration, the comparison with MCMC and the reproduction of the
published results. The documentation is also available at
<https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/>.

## Validation

- `tests/testthat` has 49 test files with 123
  [`testthat::test_that()`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_that.html)
  blocks. Their expected values were computed beforehand by independent
  Python implementations (`inst/validation/python`).
- [`inst/reproduce`](https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/bssd/tree/main/inst/reproduce)
  reproduces the numerical results of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018), Duncan
  (2026), Schnell and Ball (2016), Gould and Wang (2017), Brock et al.
  (2023), Goren et al. (2020) and Waterhouse et al. (2022): tables,
  worked examples and simulations.
- [`inst/validation`](https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/bssd/tree/main/inst/validation)
  compares
  [`bdribs_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_post.md)
  with the bdribs package;
  [`expbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/expbern_post.md),
  [`llbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/llbern_post.md),
  [`exptime_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/exptime_post.md),
  [`binbeta_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/binbeta_post.md),
  [`canary_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/canary_post.md),
  [`mapbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/mapbern_post.md)
  and
  [`multibin_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/multibin_post.md)
  with MCMC in JAGS (for
  [`canary_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/canary_post.md),
  with the Poisson likelihood) and with independent Python computations;
  the default integration grids with finer grids; and
  [`sim_oc()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/sim_oc.md)
  with an independent Python simulation.

Each item is judged as PASS (agreement within the tolerance), EXPLAINED
(a difference whose reason is registered), FAIL (a difference without a
registered reason) or INFO (no value to compare with):

| file                                | PASS | EXPLAINED | FAIL | INFO |
|:------------------------------------|-----:|----------:|-----:|-----:|
| reproduce_Brock2023.csv             |   55 |         0 |   41 |    0 |
| reproduce_Duncan2026.csv            |   15 |         6 |    0 |    7 |
| reproduce_Duncan2026_prior.csv      |   23 |         6 |    0 |    0 |
| reproduce_Duncan2026_simulation.csv |   14 |         4 |    0 |  113 |
| reproduce_Goren2020.csv             |   12 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| reproduce_Goren2020_table2.csv      |  120 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| reproduce_Gould2017.csv             |   71 |        17 |    0 |    0 |
| reproduce_Mukhopadhyay2018.csv      |   82 |         4 |    0 |    1 |
| reproduce_Schnell2016.csv           |   27 |         3 |    1 |   16 |
| reproduce_Schnell2016_table1.csv    |    2 |         4 |    0 |    0 |
| reproduce_Waterhouse2022.csv        |   11 |         0 |    1 |    2 |
| validate_bdribs_package.csv         |   35 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| validate_convergence.csv            |   19 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| validate_gould2017_author_grid.csv  |   28 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| validate_jags.csv                   |   24 |         0 |    0 |    3 |
| validate_jags_methods.csv           |   16 |         0 |    0 |    1 |
| validate_methods_python.csv         |  247 |         0 |    0 |    0 |
| validate_sim_oc.csv                 |   29 |         0 |    0 |    0 |

The reasons for the EXPLAINED items are listed in
[`inst/reproduce/results/SUMMARY.md`](https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/bssd/blob/main/inst/reproduce/results/SUMMARY.md).

## References

Ball, G. and Schnell, P. M. (2016). Blinded safety signal monitoring for
the FDA IND reporting final rule. In J. Lin et al. (eds.), *Statistical
Applications from Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine to Finance
and Business Analytics*, ICSA Book Series in Statistics, 201-209.
Springer, Cham. <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-42568-9_17>

Brock, K., Chen, C., Ho, S., Fuller, G., Woolfolk, J., McShea, C. and
Penard, N. (2023). A Bayesian method for safety signal detection in
ongoing blinded randomised controlled trials. *Pharmaceutical
Statistics*, 22(2), 378-395. <https://doi.org/10.1002/pst.2278>

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using
alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. *Journal of
Biopharmaceutical Statistics*, 36(2), 227-244.
<https://doi.org/10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532>

Goren, E., Lin, L.-A., Blaustein, R. O. and Ball, G. (2020). Bayesian
meta-analysis of safety outcomes using blinded clinical trial data.
*Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science*, 54, 1557-1565.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/s43441-020-00183-7>

Gould, A. L. and Wang, W. B. (2017). Monitoring potential adverse event
rate differences using data from blinded trials: the canary in the coal
mine. *Statistics in Medicine*, 36(1), 92-104.
<https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.7129>

Mukhopadhyay, S., Waterhouse, B., and Hartford, A. (2018). Bayesian
detection of potential risk using inference on blinded safety data.
*Pharmaceutical Statistics*, 17(6), 823-834.
<https://doi.org/10.1002/pst.1898>

Schnell, P. M. and Ball, G. (2016). A Bayesian exposure-time method for
clinical trial safety monitoring with blinded data. *Therapeutic
Innovation & Regulatory Science*, 50(6), 833-838.
<https://doi.org/10.1177/2168479016656702>

Waterhouse, B., Hartford, A., Mukhopadhyay, S., Ferguson, R. and
Hendrickson, B. A. (2022). Using the Bayesian detection of potential
risk using inference on blinded safety data (BDRIBS) method to support
the decision to refer an event for unblinded evaluation. *Pharmaceutical
Statistics*, 21(2), 372-385. <https://doi.org/10.1002/pst.2175>

# Package index

## Posterior probability of a safety signal

Posterior distributions under the models of the package, and the methods
for their results.

- [`bdribs_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_post.md)
  : Posterior probability of a safety signal under the BDRIBS model
- [`binbeta_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/binbeta_post.md)
  : Posterior of the event proportions under the blinded binomial model
- [`multibin_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/multibin_post.md)
  : Posterior of the rate ratio from blinded event counts of several
  studies
- [`canary_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/canary_post.md)
  : Posterior of the risk elevation from the total event count
- [`expbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/expbern_post.md)
  : Posterior probability of a safety signal under the EXP_BERN model
- [`llbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/llbern_post.md)
  : Posterior probability of a safety signal under the LL_BERN model
- [`exptime_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/exptime_post.md)
  : Posterior of the event rates under the exposure-time Poisson model
- [`mapbern_post()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/mapbern_post.md)
  : Posterior probability of a higher event probability on study drug
  with a meta-analytic predictive prior
- [`map_beta()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/map_beta.md)
  : Meta-analytic predictive prior of an event probability
- [`print(`*`<bssd_post>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/print.bssd_post.md)
  : Print a posterior summary for safety signal detection
- [`summary(`*`<bssd_post>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/summary.bssd_post.md)
  : Summarize a posterior for safety signal detection as a data frame

## Monitoring tools

Grids of BDRIBS results, pooled trials, decision boundaries for event
counts and their exact operating characteristics, and elicitation of
priors.

- [`bdribs_grid()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/bdribs_grid.md)
  : Posterior probabilities of the BDRIBS model on a grid of data
- [`pooled_ratio()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/pooled_ratio.md)
  : Randomization ratio of blinded data pooled from several studies
- [`signal_count()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/signal_count.md)
  : Smallest event count that gives a signal
- [`count_oc()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/count_oc.md)
  : Probability that the blinded event count reaches a critical value
- [`elicit_prior()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/elicit_prior.md)
  : Prior parameters from two quantiles

## Exposure and the log-logistic distribution

- [`time_at_risk()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/time_at_risk.md)
  : Total exposure time and total time at risk
- [`ll_cdf()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/ll_cdf.md)
  : Cumulative incidence of the log-logistic distribution
- [`ll_mu()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/ll_mu.md) :
  Location parameter of the log-logistic distribution for a given
  incidence

## Simulation

- [`sim_blinded()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/sim_blinded.md)
  : Simulate blinded clinical trial data on an adverse event
- [`sim_oc()`](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/reference/sim_oc.md)
  : Operating characteristics of the signal detection models by
  simulation

### Models

  time](https://gosukehommaex.github.io/bssd/articles/bdribs1.md):
